executiveDesks.description: C-suite and senior management workstations. Premium materials, statement aesthetic.
executiveDesks.sizingGuidance: Executive desk minimum 1800W — 2400W+ for partners and directors. L-shape preferred for dual-screen workflows.

sitStandDesks.description: Height-adjustable electric desks for ergonomic compliance and productivity.
sitStandDesks.sizingGuidance: Min 1400W for single-person workstation. 1600W standard. 1800W+ for senior staff.
sitStandDesks.upgradeValue: Add $400–$600 per desk from standard to sit-stand — 60–70% acceptance rate when framed as health investment

workstations.description: Open-plan systems for 4–20+ staff. Back-to-back, spine, cluster configurations.
workstations.bundleOpportunity: Every workstation should include a task chair recommendation

boardroomTables.description: High-impact decision-making spaces. The most visible furniture in any office.
boardroomTables.crossSell: Always quote boardroom chairs and AV credenza alongside table

receptionAreas.description: First impression zone. Highest ROI per dollar spent on brand perception.
receptionAreas.designPrinciple: Reception represents 5–10% of project budget but creates 80% of the first impression

seating.description: Task, meeting, lounge, and visitor seating across all price tiers.

subcategories.taskChairs: Full ergonomic for 8hr daily use. Look for lumbar adjustment, armrest configuration, seat depth. Certifications: AFRDI/BIFMA.
subcategories.meetingChairs: Stackable or on-castors for flexible use. Lower back height acceptable.
subcategories.loungeChairs: Reception and breakout areas. Comfort and aesthetic priority over ergonomics.
subcategories.stackableChairs: Training and event use. Commercial-grade PP plastic preferred.

seating.marginNote: Highest margin category — always include seating in every project proposal

storageFiling.description: Pedestals, filing cabinets, lockers, credenzas, overhead storage.

officePodsBooaths.description: Acoustic privacy pods for phone calls, focus work, and small collaboration.
officePodsBooaths.whenToRecommend: Any open-plan office above 20 staff — acoustic pods reduce noise complaints and improve focus productivity

industryTerminology.ABW: Activity-Based Working — staff move between zone types rather than owning fixed desks
industryTerminology.hotDesking: Unassigned desks shared on first-come basis
industryTerminology.PracticalCompletion: PC — point when builder officially hands tenancy to the client
industryTerminology.BIFMA: Business and Institutional Furniture Manufacturers Association — US-origin quality certification
industryTerminology.AFRDI: Australian Furnishing Research and Development Institute — Australian seating standard
industryTerminology.specIn: Getting specified by an architect/designer early — bypasses competitive tender
industryTerminology.mobilePedestal: Rolling under-desk storage unit with drawers and lock
industryTerminology.modestypanel: Privacy screen fixed to front of desk — hides cable tray and legs

competitorTypes: Volume retailers (Officeworks, IKEA Business) — price-focused, low service, short warranty
Grey importers — no warranty support, unknown quality, no installation
Spec furniture brands (Herman Miller, Steelcase, Knoll) — premium brand, 5–10x price premium
Local commercial suppliers — strongest competition, differentiate on service and range depth
marketDynamics.differentiationStrategy: Compete on project certainty, service quality, 6-year warranty, and local presence — never on price against volume players
marketDynamics.australianMarketSize: Commercial office furniture: AUD $2.4B annually. Growing with hybrid work driving fitout refresh cycles.
marketDynamics.hybridWorkImpact: Post-2022: offices need fewer desks but more collaboration zones. Refresh cycles shortened to 3–5 years from 7–10 years.
